leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight round-1 files prefer B015 (Katori and Ye) as the whole prize. Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce state they moved to it after reading the openings, from B023, B013 and B007 respectively, while Kroll and Lindroth held it as first choice. All five rest the case on the same elements: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice as the invention, Ye's realization at about 1e-18, independent reproduction at several laboratories, and a clean two-name credit. They differ on what they would add or tighten: Kroll and Olsson stress the unresolved status of the SI redefinition of the second; Lindroth and Olsson raise single-ion and Paris/PTB contributions; Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce want the citation worded to separate it from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. The citations written by the five differ slightly in wording (some include the 1e-18 level, Lindroth's does not).

Danielsson alone prefers B006 (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) for the sequence of a concrete prediction followed by an unexpected experimental result and the platform it created. He lists B055 and B015 as alternatives and himself flags the unresolved pairing mechanism, sample disorder and incomplete credit as limits. Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Eriksson list B006 as an alternative, which is not a preference for it in this round. Mehlig and Pearce hold it for a later year on maturity grounds; Kroll asks whether B015 needs a principled reason to omit it.

Eriksson alone prefers B055 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) for the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall effect, roughly two decades of confirmation, and an organising principle that has changed electronic-structure practice. He identifies credit as the weak point, since Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore, Balents, Roy and the ARPES work fall outside the supplied names, and notes an unresolved framing and overlap question with other topological candidates. He lists B006 and B015 as alternatives.

Johansson alone prefers B024 (Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf) as the step from macroscopic quantum circuits to engineered quantum systems with a clean theory-plus-experiment pairing. He himself raises proximity to the 2025 circuit prize, incomplete credit for Girvin, Huang and the transmon, and a possible need to recuse. He lists B015 and B010 as alternatives. Lindroth lists B024 as an alternative, with the same reservation about the 2025 prize.

areas_of_agreement: Every member who prefers B015 gives the same core account: Katori's magic-wavelength trapping as the invention and Ye's group reaching about 1e-18 as the realization, with independent reproduction at JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and NPL.
All eight preferred configurations are single-part prizes; no member proposes a two-part prize as the preferred configuration, although Kroll asks whether one should be considered.

Several members of different persuasions (Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Mehlig, Pearce) name the unresolved pairing mechanism in twisted bilayer graphene as the main reason B006 is held as an alternative or described as early.
Members who prefer B015, and Danielsson in his alternatives, treat B015 as a serious candidate whose main reservations concern framing and credit boundaries rather than the science itself.
Three members (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson) prefer different candidates, and each states the weakest point of their own choice, largely as credit incompleteness or maturity.
scientific_disputes: Whether an enabling measurement advance such as the lattice clock ranks below a discovery of new phenomena. Danielsson values prediction followed by surprise (B006); the B015 supporters regard the clock as an invention with demonstrated reach into relativistic geodesy, constants and the redefinition of the second.

Whether B015 is a distinct step from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes or a refinement of recognized work; Mehlig, Olsson, Kroll and Pearce all ask for this to be tested and Lindroth treats it as a possible incremental-in-kind judgment.
Whether B006 is a larger scientific wave than B015 (Kroll's own remark) and whether the debate over the origin of superconductivity should delay it.
Whether B055 should be framed narrowly around the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall effect or broadly around topological insulators, and how it overlaps with other topological candidates (Eriksson).
Whether the 2025 circuit prize makes B024 too close in subject matter to recognize now (Johansson, Lindroth).
attribution_disputes: B015: whether crediting only Katori and Ye is defensible when the Paris (Lemonde, Le Targat), PTB and NIST lattice work, Ludlow and Lemke, and the single-ion clock community reached comparable uncertainties by other routes (Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce).
B055: the three supplied names omit Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang (who told Molenkamp's group where to look), Fu, Moore, Balents, Roy and the ARPES work (Eriksson).
B006: the theory-plus-experiment triple leaves out other early twisted-graphene theory and parallel experimental groups (Danielsson).
B024: Girvin, Huang and the transmon contribution fall outside Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf (Johansson).

B007: Pearce notes that the individual weights of Halzen, Karle and Spiering in the IceCube discovery are not obviously established for a prize; Pearce also calls the Higgs attribution problem unresolved, though no member prefers B007 or B037 in this round.
maturity_disputes: Whether the SI redefinition of the second must be completed before honouring lattice clocks (raised by Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson; Pearce notes it is pending).
Whether twisted bilayer graphene is mature enough given the debated pairing mechanism and twist-angle and sample disorder (Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Pearce).
B055 is described by Eriksson as mature with about two decades of confirmation, but the promised dissipationless edge transport has not materialised and the case rests on conceptual influence.
B024 has long independent confirmation, but its timing relative to the 2025 prize is questioned by Johansson and Lindroth.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (prefers B024) works in circuit and waveguide QED, directs WACQT and collaborates with Chalmers colleagues including Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson; he asks whether he should recuse on B024. He records no documented tie to Blais, Wallraff or Schoelkopf.

Kroll discloses a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder (Hall: 2005 prize, frequency comb) and his work on WACQT and quantum information that makes B010 and quantum sensing close to his field; he records no tie to Katori or Ye.

Lindroth works in atomic physics and precision spectroscopy, the subfield of B015 which she ranks first; she records no collaboration with Katori or Ye, and discloses collaboration at ETH Zurich with Keller's group, not Wallraff's, relevant to B024.
Olsson works in transmission electron microscopy, the field of B013, and has moved it to an alternative; she notes that Johansson is a Chalmers colleague, with no effect on B015.

Pearce (chair) discloses field-adjacent interest in B007 (astroparticle physics) and, through CERN-based doctoral training, in B037 (Higgs), and would disclose or recuse when those are weighed; no documented tie to any candidate in B015.
Danielsson, Eriksson and Mehlig record no specific conflict.
questions_for_round2: What exact wording would a B015 citation need to separate the lattice-clock invention and realization from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and would the five B015 supporters accept the 1e-18 wording that most of their citations share?
Is crediting only Katori and Ye defensible given the Paris, PTB, NIST and single-ion contributions, and can any member state a principled line between inventor and refiner on the supplied evidence?
Is completion of the SI redefinition of the second a precondition for B015, or merely a supporting consideration?

Danielsson, Eriksson and Johansson: given that B015 is the only candidate with five explicit preferences, what specific evidence would move you toward or away from it, and does each of your own choices have a resolution for the credit gap you identified?

Does the committee judge twisted bilayer graphene (B006) premature because of the open pairing mechanism, or would it support B006 alongside or after B015, and is a two-part prize paired with B015 worth exploring given the limit of three laureates per prize?
Should Johansson recuse from deliberation on B024, and should the chair disclose the B007 and B037 interests formally before those candidates are discussed?
summary.chair_observation: Five of eight members explicitly prefer B015 in round 1, with three of them reporting a move toward it after the openings; Danielsson, Eriksson and Johansson each prefer a different single candidate (B006, B055, B024) and each names credit or maturity limits in their own choice. Shared reservations about B015 concern framing against the 2005 and 2012 prizes, the boundary of credit, and the pending redefinition of the second, none of which any member presents as decisive against the science. The count reflects only explicit round-1 configurations and does not imply how any member will vote.
